abstract: BACKGROUND: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is a rare but highly chemosensitive pregnancy-related malignancy with a strong tendency for hematogenous spread and hemorrhagic metastasis. Brain involvement occurs in a minority of patients and may present as life-threatening intracranial hemorrhage. CASE PRESENTATION: A 40-year-old Ethiopian woman presented with a sudden-onset severe headache, focal seizures, vomiting, and progressive right-sided weakness. She had a history of spontaneous abortion five months prior. Neuroimaging revealed a left frontoparietal intraparenchymal hemorrhagic mass with surrounding edema and a concomitant holohemispheric subacute subdural hematoma causing mass effect. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels were elevated to 1500 IU/L. Although lower than the levels typically observed in disseminated choriocarcinoma, modest β-hCG elevations may occur in partially regressed primary lesions or in isolated metastatic disease. The patient underwent urgent craniotomy with evacuation of the subdural hematoma and resection of a hemorrhagic intraparenchymal metastatic lesion. Histopathological examination confirmed a diagnosis of metastatic choriocarcinoma. Staging evaluation revealed pulmonary and uterine involvement, consistent with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IV disease, with a World Health Organization prognostic score of 11. She received multi-agent chemotherapy with progressive neurological recovery and normalization of β-hCG levels during follow-up. CONCLUSION: Simultaneous intraparenchymal and subdural hemorrhages can represent a rare initial presentation of metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia, even in the absence of gynecologic symptoms. Prompt measurement of serum β-hCG levels is essential for early diagnosis of unexplained intracranial hemorrhage in women of reproductive age. Early neurosurgical intervention combined with timely multi-agent chemotherapy can result in favorable outcomes, even in high-risk stage IV disease with brain metastasis.
abstract_ja: 背景:妊娠性絨毛性腫瘍は稀だが、化学療法への感受性が高い妊娠関連の悪性腫瘍であり、血行性の進展と出血性転移の傾向が強い。脳転移は少数の患者にみられ、生命を脅かす頭蓋内出血として発症しうる。症例提示:40歳のエチオピア人女性が、突然発症した激しい頭痛、焦点性痙攣、嘔吐、進行性の右片麻痺で受診した。5か月前に自然流産の既往があった。神経画像検査で、左前頭頭頂部の脳実質内出血性腫瘤と周囲の浮腫、ならびに半球全体に及ぶ亜急性硬膜下血腫が認められ、腫瘤効果を生じていた。血清β-ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(β-hCG)は1500 IU/Lに上昇していた。播種性絨毛癌で通常みられるレベルより低いが、部分的に退縮した原発巣や孤立性転移病変では、わずかなβ-hCGの上昇がみられることがある。患者は緊急開頭術を受け、硬膜下血腫の除去と出血性の脳実質内転移病変の切除を行った。病理組織学的検査で転移性絨毛癌と確定した。病期評価では肺と子宮の病変が認められ、FIGO病期IVに相当し、世界保健機関(WHO)の予後スコアは11であった。多剤併用化学療法を受け、経過観察中に神経学的回復が進み、β-hCGも正常化した。結論:脳実質内出血と硬膜下出血の同時発生は、婦人科症状がない場合でも、転移性妊娠性絨毛性腫瘍の稀な初発症状となりうる。生殖年齢の女性で原因不明の頭蓋内出血がみられた場合は、血清β-hCGの速やかな測定が早期診断に不可欠である。脳転移を伴う高リスクのFIGO病期IVであっても、早期の脳神経外科的介入と適時の多剤併用化学療法により良好な転帰が得られうる。
